#### §31: Utilities

| ID | Spec | Ann. | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-31.1 | §31 | — | **The utilities are spec §31 with their own decision series D-31 and view `s31` (UTIL-0; `plan/utilities.md` Q7, owner's approval 2026-11-14).** §31 specifies what callers depend on (command names and paths, options, output formats, exit codes, files read and written, environment) for ldconfig, ldd, getent, getconf, iconv, locale, localedef, zic, zdump, tzselect, gencat and pldd, and what is not provided (§31.14); each item cites POSIX, a man page, RFC 8536, Appendix D, or a case of `spec/behaviour/utilities.glibc.txt` (black-box probe `tools/probe/util_spec.sh`, run as an ordinary user on the reference). A behaviour the design decided differently is marked **Liella rule**, with a differences row and a D-31 decision. Tooling: `cargo xtask stubs` reads the sections after §30 (§30, the pattern catalogue, gives no clauses: `spec::NO_CLAUSES`), so §31's clauses are `s31_<sub>_<field>_<n>` and their stubs are `crates/core/tests/s31_utilities_clauses.rs`; `spec/schedule.tsv` gives §31 to the track `UTIL` (from VAL, started 2026-11-14), so each UTIL story specifies its clauses in place. |
| D-31.2 | §31 | — | **Shape of the utilities: a library per domain holding both sides of each file format, one executable per domain, ldconfig freestanding and static (`plan/utilities.md` §3-§4, Q1 and Q2; owner's approval 2026-11-14).** Each format's writer lives in the crate of its reader (the loader cache in `liella-ld`, TZif in a `liella-tz` crate shared with the C library's reader, locales in a `liella-locale` crate, catalogs beside `catopen`'s reader), so reader and writer are tested against each other. `liella-tz` answers as zic, zdump and tzselect and `liella-locale` as locale, localedef, locale-gen, update-locale and validlocale, chosen by `argv[0]`; a domain with one command is a plain program. ldconfig is a freestanding static program with no C library dependency (dpkg needs it before any package operation and while `libc6` is replaced); Liella's `libc-bin` declares interest in the dpkg `ldconfig` trigger. UTIL-SHAPE measures the domain executables against separate programs (start-up instructions, faults, size); a domain that costs more falls back to separate programs (a build change only). Public interfaces: the commands and the file formats; a public Rust `tz` API in `liella-native` after UTIL-10 (UTIL-16); a `locale` API deferred; no new C ABI until a C consumer asks (D-X.10). |
| D-31.3 | §31, App. D | — | **On-disk formats stay compatible (owner's ruling 2026-11-14).** The utilities write TZif per RFC 8536 (zic, §31.9), the loader cache in the Appendix D.3.1 new format with the D.3.2 extensions (ldconfig, §31.2), the locale directory and archive of D.1 (localedef, §31.8), and the catalog format of D.2 (gencat, §31.12), so files written by Liella's tools and by the reference's are interchangeable, and coexistence systems and direct readers keep working. A Liella-native format (for example for the CLDR-derived locale set) is proposed only with a measured gain and a decision of its own. |
| D-31.4 | §31.1, §31.2 | — | **Identity strings of the utilities are Liella's (`plan/utilities.md` Q3; owner's approval 2026-11-14).** The first line of `--version` is `<command> (Liella <version>) 2.39`, the bug-report line of `--help` names Liella's channel, and ldconfig's tag 0 text (`Cache generated by:` in `-p`) names Liella's ldconfig; the trailing ABI level `2.39` stays, so scripts that read the version number see the ABI they get. No compatibility option: the banner states who built the program, and a script that tells C libraries apart (for example by `ldd --version`) must see the truth. The mirror scan of LIELLA-SYSTEM-LIBC-PLAN counts scripts that match the reference's banner text before UTIL-3 ships; a match it finds is raised with the owner. The transcript harness (UTIL-1) masks identity strings when it compares. `getconf GNU_LIBC_VERSION` follows `confstr` (§24), not this decision. |
| D-31.5 | §31.14 | — | **Not installed: `iconvconfig`, `/etc/bindresvport.blacklist`, `sprof`, `sotruss`, `mtrace`, `nscd` (`plan/utilities.md` Q4, owner's approval 2026-11-14; R8).** `iconvconfig` indexes conversion modules and Liella has none (D-6.8: charsets are built in or read from the installed charmaps); `/etc/bindresvport.blacklist` serves Sun RPC, which Liella does not implement; the `libc-devtools` commands have no caller in the caller search of the design; `nscd` is dropped (R8; Liella's name-service cache is in the library, D-16.10). No compatibility option: there is nothing for a restored command to act on. Revisited if the mirror scan of LIELLA-SYSTEM-LIBC-PLAN finds callers. gencat and pldd are kept (UTIL-14, UTIL-15). |
| D-31.6 | §31.2 | — | **`ldconfig -c old` and `-c compat` are refused (`plan/utilities.md` Q5, owner's approval 2026-11-14; #941).** ldconfig prints a message naming the new format as the one it writes and exits nonzero without writing anything; `-c new` (the default) is accepted. No compatibility option: Liella's loader reads only the new format (D-27.16, #941), so an old-format cache would be ignored by the loader it serves. The reference writes the old format on request (probe `ldconfig-c-old`). |
| D-31.7 | §31.3 | SEC | **ldd never runs the operand's code or another interpreter (`plan/utilities.md` Q6, owner's approval 2026-11-14).** ldd lists each operand through Liella's loader in list mode (`--list`, D-27.16), which maps the dependencies and runs none of their code, so ldd and the loader agree on every resolution. For an operand whose `PT_INTERP` is not Liella's loader, ldd lists by Liella's rules and says so on standard error. So ldd on an untrusted file runs none of its code. No compatibility option: running an untrusted file's code is the behaviour this rule exists to remove. `-v` reads the version needs itself. `-d`, `-r` and `-u` need relocation processing, so they are refused with a message until DL-10. |
| D-31.8 | §31.14 | — | **The `locales` commands are Liella's own (`plan/utilities.md` Q8, owner's approval 2026-11-14; R1).** `locale-gen`, `update-locale` and `validlocale` are reimplemented inside `liella-locale` from their man pages (locale-gen(8), update-locale(8)) and the files they use (`/etc/locale.gen`, `/etc/default/locale`, `SUPPORTED`); they compile in process, one parse of each charmap and shared source for all requested locales, in parallel. Counters per locale against one `localedef` process per locale decide any speed claim (UTIL-13). Their interface clauses are added with UTIL-13. |
| D-31.9 | §31.2 | SEC | **ldconfig writes a deterministic cache, replaces it atomically, and treats every file it reads as untrusted (`plan/utilities.md` §4; owner's approval 2026-11-14).** Entries are in the Appendix D.3.3 order, ties broken by configuration order and then path bytes, and directory listings are sorted, so identical trees give byte-identical caches on any file system. The cache is written to a temporary file in its own directory, synced, and renamed over the old one. Every ELF file is bounds-checked and never mapped executable. `-r ROOT` resolves every path inside ROOT with `openat2(RESOLVE_IN_ROOT)` and needs no privilege (the reference also succeeds for an ordinary user, probe `ldconfig-r-user`); `chroot` only where `openat2` is missing. An auxiliary cache (under `/var/cache/ldconfig/`, Liella's own file) only if UTIL-3's counters show a gain. |
| D-31.10 | §31 | — | The utilities' transcript harness (UTIL-1) is `cargo xtask transcript` in xtask/src/transcript/, not scripts under validation/: xtask is std-only with no third-party code, already links liella-ld (whose writer builds a transcript's `cache:` items and whose reader backs the `ldconfig -p` stub until UTIL-3), and its comparator is Rust with unit tests that plants check. Transcripts are data (validation/transcripts/<utility>/*.transcript; format in docs/transcripts.md): argv with argv[0] the bare command name on both sides, the exact environment, stdin, the private root's items, an optional unprivileged user and mount namespace with binds, and the reference's outcome written by `record`. `check` compares Liella with the reference and the reference with the record (a stale record fails); status, stdout, stderr and every written path are compared separately, so text on the wrong stream is a mismatch. Normalisation is only the private root's path (`@ROOT@`) unless a transcript adds a `normalise:` literal with its reason. A host without user namespaces prints SKIPPED with the reason. |
| D-31.11 | §31.2 | — | **ldconfig's engine rules beyond D-31.9 (UTIL-3, `plan/utilities.md` §4; engine `crates/ld/src/ldconfig/`).** (1) A soname link is replaced atomically: a new link under a temporary name in the same directory, renamed over the old one, so a concurrent reader sees the old link or the new one, never none. (2) Directory listings, glob matches and soname groups are sorted before use, so the same tree gives the same messages, links and byte-identical cache on any file system (`listing_order_changes_nothing`, `random_configurations_end_cleanly`). (3) ELF headers are read with bounds-checked positioned reads of the needed bytes only; nothing is mapped. (4) Only ELF files of the native class, byte order and machine are entered in the cache; other ELF files are skipped silently (an open question for multilib systems, raised by UTIL-LDCONFIG-3). (5) An `include` that would re-enter a configuration file already being read (found by file identity), or nest deeper than the engine's depth limit, is refused with one message naming the file and line (`include of <file> would loop (include cycle), ignored`); the rest of the configuration is read as usual and the exit status does not change (`include_cycles_end_with_a_message`). (6) A glibc-hwcaps cache entry whose file name is not its soname stores the key as its own string (the cache writer, `write_hwcaps_key_other_than_the_file_name`). (7) `-l` (link individual libraries) is refused with a message and exit 1 until it is implemented; it is a gap, not a design choice. |
| D-31.12 | §31.2 | — | **The shipped ldconfig is a static PIE with no interpreter, its own start, a bump arena and a system-call file system (UTIL-3, D-31.2, D-31.9).** `cargo xtask so` links `crates/ldconfig-bin` into `target/liella/ldconfig` and refuses it unless it has no `PT_INTERP` and passes the loader's link invariant (L14-1: nothing undefined, no `DT_NEEDED`, only RELATIVE/RELR relocations); it starts as ld.so does (`machine/entry.S` built with `-DLIELLA_LDCONFIG`, the loader's self-relocator), so dpkg can run it while libc6 is replaced and from outside a `--root`. Its allocator is a bump arena over anonymous mappings (the last block grows and shrinks in place; other freed blocks stay until exit): one short-lived, single-threaded process needs no general heap, and the product heap needs a thread block the program does not set up. Its file system (`liella_ld::ldconfig::sysfs`) goes through the kernel `Sys` trait: with `-r ROOT` every path is opened with `openat2(RESOLVE_IN_ROOT)` below a descriptor of ROOT and the last component is acted on through its parent's descriptor, so links, reads and the cache stay inside ROOT with no privilege; a ROOT that cannot be opened makes every operation fail with its error. libc-bin ships it as `/usr/sbin/ldconfig` and runs it on the dpkg `ldconfig` trigger (`-r "$DPKG_ROOT"` when set). Proof: the 12 committed transcripts pass through the binary against the reference (`the_shipped_ldconfig_passes_the_transcripts`); plants `handoff/UTIL-LDCONFIG-4-plants.txt`. |
| D-31.13 | §31.2 | — | **ldconfig links and records the i386 and x32 objects of a multilib x86-64 system with their own type's flags; when one directory holds files of one soname but different types, the highest version wins and its type is recorded, whatever order the directory lists them in (UTIL-3, ruling #5922).** `Arch::LDCONFIG_TYPES` names the ELF types the engine accepts with their cache flags: on x86-64, ELF64 `EM_X86_64` (`0x0303`), ELF32 `EM_386` (`0x0003`) and ELF32 `EM_X86_64` (x32, `0x0803`); any other class, byte order or machine is skipped silently, as before. Probe (`validation/transcripts/ldconfig/foreign-class.transcript`, against the reference): i386 and x32 objects get their soname links and `-v` lines like native ones, cache entries `0x3` and `0x803`, no message. Second probe (same soname, a native and an i386 file in one directory, each case with private roots on ext4 and on tmpfs and in both creation orders): the reference always links the highest version, but its cache flags and its message `libraries <a> and <b> in directory <dir> have same soname but different type.` change with the directory's listing order (an entry can carry the flags of the file the link does not name). That outcome depends on the file system, so it is not a committed transcript. Liella's rule follows §31.2's determinism rule: listings are sorted, the highest version under the D.3.3 comparison wins the link, the entry carries the winner's flags (the type of the file the loader opens through the link), and each other-type file of that soname is reported as `libraries <other> and <winner> in directory <dir> have same soname but different type.`. The link always matches the reference. The message text is the reference's, but the reference printed it only in the listing order where the winner came last, and then its entry carried the loser's flags; Liella prints the message in every order and records the winner's flags, a combination the reference did not show in either order. Test: `foreign_class_objects_are_recorded_with_their_type` (crates/ld/tests/ldconfig.rs, both listing orders). |
| D-31.14 | §31.5 | — | **getconf is a static C front end over Liella's `libc.a`, and its name table is generated from `spec/abi/getconf.tsv` joined with `spec/abi/sysconf.tsv` (UTIL-5, `plan/utilities.md` §4).** `csys/util/getconf.c` is linked by `cargo xtask so` as a static PIE (`liella-rcrt1.o`, `libc.a`) into `target/liella/getconf` and shipped as `/usr/bin/getconf` in libc-bin. Static rather than dynamic: the values are Liella's `sysconf`, `confstr` and `pathconf` in every root and on every build host, with no loader in the way, so the transcripts prove the shipped program itself; it is the same program a dynamic build would be, so a later switch to dynamic (one link line) needs only UTIL-SHAPE's counters. `spec/abi/getconf.tsv` holds the 414 names the reference accepts (320 listed by `-a`, in its order, and 94 accepted but unlisted, such as `TRACE` and `VERSION`), each with the constant it answers from and whether its value prints unsigned (`ULONG_MAX`); the kinds and numbers come from `sysconf.tsv`, the table the library's own answers are generated from (D-24.6), so a name cannot name a constant the library does not have and the build stops if it does. The name set and every behaviour were settled by black-box probes of the reference (candidate names formed from every constant in `sysconf.tsv`); `-v` accepts any specification and does not change a value, as the reference does on x86-64. `GNU_LIBC_VERSION` is `confstr`'s text. `--help` prints the usage paragraph without a bug-reporting address and `--version` prints `getconf (Liella) <version>` (identity strings, plan/utilities.md Q3; no transcript compares them). |
| D-31.15 | §31.3 | DD | **ldd's front end (UTIL-4; builds on D-31.7).** `ldd` is a static PIE over `libc.a` (`csys/util/ldd.c`, shipped by libc-bin at `/usr/bin/ldd`). It reads each operand's ELF headers itself: not an x86-64 ELF64 file or no `PT_DYNAMIC` gives `not a dynamic executable` on standard error and status 1; no `DT_NEEDED` gives `statically linked` (static and static-pie programs); otherwise it runs Liella's loader on the operand with `LD_TRACE_LOADED_OBJECTS=1` and prints the loader's listing. Options, messages, `<file>:` headers for several operands and exit statuses follow the reference's observable behaviour (28 transcripts in `validation/transcripts/ldd/`, plus the swap-root comparison in `tools/deb/swap-cmds.sh` on the distribution's own libc-linked programs and initramfs-tools' `copy_exec`). `-v` prints `Version information:` only when some listed object has version needs, from `DT_VERNEED` read by ldd itself. `--version` prints `ldd (Liella) 2.39`, as getent and getconf name themselves. The listing is the loader's as it is (the interpreter rule is the loader's: D-27.56; the interim filter of ruling #6043 is removed). The comparison masks only a line's final ` (0x<hex>)` load address, which changes from run to run on both systems. (Amended by D-27.56.) |
| D-31.16 | §31.6 | IMPL | **The `iconv` command is a dynamic C front end over `iconv(3)`; each input is converted whole and the output written at the end; `-l` lists what `iconv_open` accepts (UTIL-7, `plan/utilities.md` §4).** `csys/util/iconv.c` is built by `cargo xtask so` as getent is (`target/niji/iconv` for libc-bin's `/usr/bin/iconv`, a test link on the tree's loader for the transcripts). It reads each operand whole and converts it with its own `iconv` calls, so a character split across two files is incomplete in the first, and collects the output, written once at exit (also after an error), so `-o` may name an input and an empty output creates no file: all as black-box probes of the reference showed (`validation/transcripts/iconv/`). `-c` appends `IGNORE` to the target's suffixes and continues past `EILSEQ` while the library makes progress. `-l` prints the built-in names (`csys/util/iconv-names.h`, held equal to `niji::iconv::builtin_names` by a core test) and every file stem of `/usr/share/i18n/charmaps` that `iconv_open` accepts, sorted, once each, as `NAME//` (`NAME/` for a name holding `/`). Charmap alias names are not listed yet: the front end has no gzip reader (open question in the UTIL-7 hand-back). Identity strings follow §31.1 (`iconv (libniji) 2.39`, no distribution bug-report line). |
